source.title: Rapid Convergence of the Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm: Isoperimetry Suffices

checks.paper_location: Official proceedings main PDF and supplemental archive
checks.claim: The official supplement contains the complete 29-page camera-ready PDF, including Appendices B.2.1 and B.2.2.
checks.note: The archive member is langevin_neurips_camera_ready.pdf. Appendix pages 16-19 were inspected and agree with the author-hosted full version at https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/wibisono/VW19.pdf. The official supplement is a ZIP, not a standalone Supplemental.pdf.

checks.paper_location: Sections 2.1-2.2, equations (1)-(4), pages 3-4
checks.claim: The LSI normalization is \(2\alpha H_\nu(\rho)\le J_\nu(\rho)\).
checks.note: The code uses actual extended KL and the squared relative score. For normalized \(\rho=r\nu\), KL is identified with \(\int r\log r\,d\nu\). The endpoint retains separate finiteness proofs; the total real-conversion aliases alone do not express finiteness.

checks.paper_location: Section 2.2, equations (2) and (4), page 4
checks.claim: The functional inequality applies to density tests.
checks.note: IsLogSobolev tests strictly positive C¹ relative probability densities. The complete proof constructs its actual Gaussian relative density in that class at every positive time, with finite Fisher information; LSI then gives finite actual KL. The compatibility proof likewise constructs its normalized bounded exponential tests. Thus the final theorem needs no extension or approximation beyond the original declared LSI test class.

checks.paper_location: Section 3, equation (11); Appendix B.2.1, equations (28)-(29), pages 5 and 17
checks.claim: \(X_t=X_0-t\nabla U(X_0)+\sqrt{2t}\,Z\), with independent \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\).
checks.note: The actual measure update is the pushforward of the independent product of the current law and stdGaussian. Zero-time and step-endpoint identities are proved. InterpolationDensity identifies the exact mixture and Gibbs-relative laws, and GaussianWeakEquation proves the actual kernel weak equation. The dimension is finrank over the reals; dimension zero is handled separately in the final theorem.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, after equation (33), page 19
checks.claim: \(\mathbb E\lVert X_t-X_0\rVert^2=t^2\mathbb E\lVert\nabla U(X_0)\rVert^2+2tn\).
checks.note: The proof checks the standard Gaussian second moment, zero mean, independent-product cross-term cancellation, and square integrability. It requires a finite squared-gradient moment, not a second moment of \(X_0\). Dimension zero is included.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Gaussian interpolation preceding equation (30), pages 17-18
checks.claim: At every positive time the actual Gaussian interpolation has the explicit positive finite Gaussian mixture density and its normalized Gibbs-relative density.
checks.note: The explicit actual mixture is everywhere strictly positive, finite and normalized. GaussianEntropy differentiates the spatial kernel under the probability integral to obtain C¹ relative densities, proves the Gaussian posterior score identity and Fisher bound, and applies the original LSI to prove finite actual KL. GaussianTimeDerivative and GaussianWeakEquation prove the time derivative and its actual weak equation.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, entropy calculation preceding equation (32), page 18
checks.claim: Density differentiation and integration by parts produce the entropy derivative.
checks.note: The complete route uses bounded smooth log primitives Φ_m, the actual spacetime L¹ kernel derivative and pointwise FTC/Fubini. Spatial dominated convergence identifies both entropy endpoints; a common compact-time energy majorant permits dominated convergence of the flux. GaussianEntropyIdentity proves an exact actual-KL integral identity, local absolute continuity and the raw Gaussian entropy derivative almost everywhere. Earlier LocalEntropyRegularity interfaces remain available but are not hypotheses of the final theorem.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equations (30)-(32), page 18
checks.claim: The frozen-drift equation determines entropy production.
checks.note: GaussianWeakEquation derives the component flux divergence and global spatial integration by parts for every bounded C¹ test with square-integrable gradient. GaussianEntropyIdentity proves those admissibility conditions for χ_m(log r_t) and removes the truncation by dominated convergence. GaussianScorePairing identifies the averaged component score with the actual mixture score. No weak-equation or unbounded-test admissibility premise occurs in the final theorem.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, integrating-factor entropy comparison, pages 18-19
checks.claim: The affine scalar entropy comparison requires derivatives only in the open interval and continuity at the endpoints.
checks.note: IntegratedEntropy proves affine comparison for locally absolutely continuous entropy with a differential inequality only almost everywhere on positive-time intervals. The initial endpoint uses an explicitly constructed continuous upper envelope M(t) with M(0)=H(0), rather than assuming entropy continuity or derivatives at zero. InteriorEntropy retains the earlier pointwise derivative/endpoint-continuity comparison as a separate reusable lemma.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equation (33), page 18
checks.claim: Young's inequality leaves the Fisher coefficient \(-3/4\).
checks.note: The actual Gaussian entropy derivative is negative Fisher information plus the joint frozen gradient-error/score pairing. Both factors are square integrable. The pointwise estimate ⟨a,b⟩ ≤ ‖a‖²+‖b‖²/4 leaves the coefficient −3/4, and the proved actual Gaussian displacement energy supplies L²(t²G0+2td).

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equation (33) and its following displacement calculation, pages 18-19
checks.claim: The joint gradient-error energy is bounded by \(L^2\) times displacement energy.
checks.note: frozen_gradient_error_energy proves integrability and the bound \(L^2(t^2G_0+2tn)\) on the actual independent product law. No drift-error estimate is assumed by that lemma.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, equations (31)-(33), page 18
checks.claim: The entropy cross term can be evaluated under the joint law of \(X_0\) and \(X_t\).
checks.note: ConditionalDrift constructs a measurable state-space conditional mean with Jensen and flux identities. The final convergence proof uses the equivalent actual joint Gaussian formulation directly: GaussianScorePairing averages the component Gaussian score, so a jointly time-measurable choice of conditional error field is unnecessary. Both routes preserve the same joint gradient discrepancy and its exact energy.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Lemma 9, page 16
checks.claim: \(\mathbb E_\nu\lVert\nabla U\rVert^2\le nL\).
checks.note: GibbsScore proves the sharp target score moment and square integrability from differentiability, a Lipschitz gradient and finite normalization, using translation invariance and a sub-Gaussian score MGF rather than a Hessian. The auxiliary GradientMoment transport comparison remains valid for supplied couplings. The final theorem instead uses EntropyMoment to derive the current-law score moment directly from finite KL, avoiding LSI-to-Talagrand entirely.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.1, Lemmas 9-10, pages 16-17; Section 2.2.1
checks.claim: \(G_\rho\le(4L^2/\alpha)H_\nu(\rho)+2nL\).
checks.note: Gaussian averaging of the directional Gibbs-score MGF proves ∫exp(‖∇U‖²/(4L))dν ≤2^(d/2)≤exp(d/2). A proved entropy variational inequality first derives gradient square integrability, then Gμ≤4L KL(μ|ν)+2dL. The compatibility α≤L yields the required coefficient 4L²/α. Thus the exact estimate follows from finite KL and the original smoothness/LSI assumptions, without an entropy-cost coupling or transport theorem.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3 and Theorem 2; end of Appendix B.2.1 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 6 and 19
checks.claim: The step restriction is \(0<h\le\alpha/(4L^2)\).
checks.note: The stated step restriction is unchanged. Compatibility.logSobolev_constant_le_smoothness derives α≤L from the original LSI and smoothness in positive dimension, using bounded exponential tests, a bounded-test variance consequence, a Gibbs score integration-by-parts identity and sinusoidal tests. The final theorem handles dimension zero by uniqueness of probability laws. Positive α and L remain explicit assumptions; compatibility is no longer an extra premise.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Lemma 3, equation (12); Appendix B.2.1, final scalar calculation, pages 6 and 19
checks.claim: \(H(h)\le e^{-\alpha h}H(0)+6h^2nL^2\).
checks.note: The conclusion and step constants match. Lean sets \(A=(4L^2/\alpha)H(0)+2nL\) and obtains uniform forcing \(b=(\alpha/4)H(0)+(5/2)hnL^2\). Exact affine comparison with \(a=3\alpha/2\), \((1-e^{-ah})/a\le h\), and \(e^{-3x/2}+x/4\le e^{-x}\), where \(x=\alpha h\), give the stronger noise coefficient \(5/2\) before relaxing it to \(6\). The source instead uses a \(3hnL^2\) forcing term, an integrating factor, \(e^c\le1+2c\), and multiplicative exponential absorption.

checks.paper_location: Appendix B.2.2, first displayed bound, page 19
checks.claim: Iteration yields \(H_k\le e^{-\alpha hk}H_0+8hnL^2/\alpha\).
checks.note: The scalar recurrence is iterated using the existing affine recurrence lemmas. The exact helper also retains the finite-horizon factor \(1-e^{-\alpha hk}\). The final constant \(8\) follows from \(1-e^{-x}\ge3x/4\) for \(0\le x\le1/4\). Lean proves that denominator estimate from \(e^x\ge1+x\) and a reciprocal bound.

checks.paper_location: Section 3.1, Theorem 2, page 6
checks.claim: The published conclusion concerns the actual ULA laws.
checks.note: UnconditionalTheorem proves the bound for the actual independent-Gaussian ULA laws from a differentiable potential with Lipschitz gradient, original target LSI, positive constants, the stated step restriction and finite initial KL. Its dependency chain constructs the density, time/space regularity, actual weak equation, admissible entropy test, finite Fisher/KL, initial endpoint majorant, gradient moment and compatibility, then derives and iterates the recurrence. Older conditional endpoints retain their exact hypotheses as reusable interfaces.

checks.paper_location: Sections 2.1 and 3.1; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.2.2, pages 3, 6 and 19
checks.claim: Gaussian initialization is an example; the theorem also states an accuracy threshold.
checks.note: The initial law is any probability law with finite actual KL; no Gaussian initialization, smooth initial density, initial Fisher information, state second moment, analytic interpolation data or moment premise is required. Finite KL is proved at every ULA iterate. The separate logarithmic iteration threshold for a requested accuracy δ and a stationary-bias corollary are not exported here as dedicated LSI theorems.

checks.paper_location: Positive-time interpolation and the initial endpoint; formal proof variation
checks.claim: The initial entropy endpoint follows from an explicit continuous upper envelope for the actual interpolation.
checks.note: Data processing controls KL(μP_t|νP_t). A Gaussian square completion bounds d(νP_t)/dν by δ^(-d/2)exp[t‖∇U‖²/(4δ)], δ=1−4tL>0. The proved likelihood chain rule and propagated score moment give H(t)≤H(0)−(d/2)logδ+[t/(4δ)](2(1+L²t²)G0+4tdL²). This explicit function is continuous at zero with value H(0). The scalar comparison therefore starts at arbitrary positive time and sends it to zero without assuming entropy continuity or initial density regularity.

checks.paper_location: Section 2.3.1, Theorem 1; Appendix B.1.3, pages 5 and 16
checks.claim: Continuous Langevin entropy decays at rate \(2\alpha\).
checks.note: The continuous-time comparison uses \(e^{-2\alpha t}\), distinct from the discrete factor \(e^{-\alpha hk}\). EntropyFlow derives actual-KL decay given an admissible density path and an explicit dissipation identity; it does not construct a Langevin SDE law or prove Talagrand's inequality.

verdict: The complete actual-law ULA theorem is formalized from target LSI, differentiability with a Lipschitz gradient, positive constants, the stated step restriction, and finite initial KL. The actual Gaussian density, Fisher and KL finiteness, time derivative, global weak equation, bounded-log entropy identity, initial endpoint, score moment and compatibility are all derived in its dependency chain. The update, LSI normalization, rate and constants 6 and 8 agree with the 2019 theorem. The direct entropy/score moment estimate, bounded-test compatibility proof, bounded-log spacetime chain rule and initial entropy upper envelope are documented proof variations. Older conditional path interfaces remain accurately displayed; a continuous Langevin SDE construction, a separate accuracy threshold and stationary corollaries are outside the exported discrete ULA theorem.
